Figure 1:We introduceVideoMaMa++, a mask-guided video matting framework that recovers fine-grained details (e.g., hair strands) and scales reliably to long videos.
(a) Per-frame qualitative results on diverse in-the-wild videos.
(b) Long-video matting results: VideoMaMaLim et al. (2026), which processes videos in chunks, fails to maintain consistency across chunk boundaries (red boxes), whereas VideoMaMa++ produces mattes that are both finely detailed and temporally consistent.

Figure 2:Overview of the VideoMaMa++ training and inference.(Top)During training, RGB frames are paired with either a binary mask or the ground-truth alpha matte as guide input, encoded into separate token streams by a frozen VAE encoderℰ\mathcal{E}, and tagged with a refine token (R) or preserve token (P). The DiT processes both modes jointly within a single clip, supervised against the ground-truth matte.(Bottom)At inference, long videos are processed in a sliding-window manner. Each chunk receives the refine token on its non-overlapping frames and the preserve token on its overlap frames, which carry the previous chunk’s predicted matte. A globally selected reference anchor frame is additionally supplied as preserve input to every chunk, providing a stable anchor that prevents error accumulation across the sequence.

Figure 3:Long-video temporal consistency.Qualitative comparison between VideoMaMa++ and other methods. The comparison methods exhibits visible flickering at chunk boundaries or struggles to capture fine-grained details, while VideoMaMa++ produces smooth transitions across chunks while still capturing fine-grained details that emerge in later chunks.

Figure 6:Annotation noise in AM-2KLi et al. (2022).The ground-truth alpha mattes in AM-2K often miss fine-grained internal details, that VideoMaMa++ correctly recovers. Because MAD averages pixel-wise error over the entire image, these missing details penalize accurate predictions and inflate the reported error.
MAD-T, computed only within the transition region, isolates the matting quality that actually matters and avoids the bias introduced by such annotation gaps.
